reason: Conversation 2's framing of its question ('controls, back or vents') surfaced the decisive safety fact - the browned, warm wall switch - and it responded correctly: fire risk, both switch/supply and cooker need inspection, don't remove the cover or tighten anything, electrician or cooker engineer before any use. Conversation 1 never asked about the switch, lights or crackle, so it unknowingly told the homeowner to isolate at the very cooker switch that is scorched and warm, and encouraged sliding the cooker out to inspect the rear cable, which the homeowner can't safely do. Conversation 1 did give an honest, appropriately uncertain list of causes and sensible repair-vs-replace advice, and Conversation 2 was abrupt and over-cautious on the opener and did not explicitly re-emphasise isolating at the consumer unit rather than the damaged switch in its final turn, which keeps the margin slight.
